High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1. Appellants have preferred this miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act") being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 7.7.2014 passed in Claim Case No.11/2012 by the Addl. Member, MACT, Garoth, District Mandsaur, whereby compensation of sum of Rs.2,66,000/- with interest of 6% per annum has been awarded in favour of the appellant Kavribai and claim petition filed by the appellants No.2 to 4 has been rejected.

2. Brief and relevant facts of the case are that on 30.12.2011 deceased Mangilal along with Balaram were returning from Melkheda to village Khajuri, at that time respondent No.1 Ishwarlal, who is the drive of the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.MP14-BD-0213 rashly and negligently drove the vehicle and coming from wrong side NNEUTRAL CITATION NO.2024:MPHC-IND:23399 dashed the deceased's bike, due to which Mangilal and Balaram both of them sustained fatal injuries and later on they have been died.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of the vehicle and at the time of accident vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.

3. The appellants had filed claim petition before the below Tribunal under Section 166 of MV Act by stating that they are dependents of the deceased Mangilal and at the time of accident deceased was agriculturist and also working as milk vendor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the death of the deceased, all the appellants were deprived from his income.
Therefore, they have filed petition claiming compensation of Rs.28,22,000/- with interest.

4. Respondents No.1 and 2 denied the claim averments by stating that no accident has taken place Smt.Kavribai vs Ishwarlal on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50430610/
1 by the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3-insurance company and respondent No.1 was having valid and effective driving licence.
Respondent No.3 also denied all the claim averments by stating in its written statement that respondent No.1 was not having any valid licence for driving Tempo Traveller.
The cover note was not issued by the insurance company.

The aforesaid cover note has been missing from 8.7.2011 from the Hinduja Complex and matter has been reported to the Police Station - Devendra Nagar, Raipur and also published the same in the newspaper.
At the time of accident vehicle was not insured with respondent No.3.
The missing cover note has been misused.

The vehicle was being driven in v i o l a t i o n o f t h e t e r m s a n d c o n d i t i o n s o f i n s u r a n c e N N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N NO.2024:MPHC-IND:23399 policy, therefore, the insurance company is not liable for any compensation.

5. On the basis of the aforesaid pleadings, the below Tribunal has framed the issues and after recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.2,66,000/- with 6% interest per annum only in favour of the appellant Kavribai and claim petition in respect of appellants No.2 to 4 has been rejected.
Being aggrieved by the same, appellants have preferred this appeal.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is against the law and facts.
Appellants No.2 to 4 are the sons of the deceased and they are dependent upon him.
Therefore, below tribunal has committed error in rejecting their claim.
The below tribunal has erred in deducting 50% as contributory negligence because doctor who has performed the postmortem, has found some liquor smell from the undigested food.
Nothing has been proved that deceased was riding the motorcycle rashly and negligently.
Therefore, the findings in this regard are not sustainable.

The below tribunal has erred in assessing income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month and also erred in awarding less compensation towards funeral expenses,
loss of estate, loss of love and affection, consortium, parental guidance etc.

Hence, he prays that the compensation amount be enhanced and the claim of appellants No.2 to 4 be accepted.
NNEUTRAL CITATION NO.2024:MPHC-IND:23399 7.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by contending that the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just,
adequate and proper and not deserve for any interference.
8.
Nobody has appeared on behalf of respondents No.1 and 2 despite service of notice at the time of final argument.
9. Both the parties heard at length and perused the entire record with due care.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that appellants No.2 to 4 are the sons of deceased Mangilal and they are dependent upon the deceased's income, therefore, they are entitled to get share in the compensation amount, but appellants No.2 to 4 are the major songs of the deceased.

From the statement of Kavribai (AW-3) before the below tribunal, it is proved that appellants No.2 Smt.Kavribai vs Ishwarlal on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50430610/
2 to 4 are doing their separate agriculture work and her husband during his lifetime made partition between three sons and as per their share they are doing farming upon it.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, on the basis of the aforesaid, trial court has rightly held that appellants No.2 to 4 are not dependent upon the deceased Mangilal and are not entitled for any compensation.
11. So far as the claim amount is concerned, below tribunal has considered the income of the deceased Mangilal Rs.4,500/- per month.
Claimants did not file any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
In view of the aforesaid, there is no reason to disbelieve the NNEUTRAL CITATION NO.2024:MPHC-IND:23399 finding given by the below Tribunal.
Below tribunal has already considered all other aspects regarding the compensation in different heads, therefore, no need to enhance any amount.

12. So far as the issue of contributory negligence is concerned, as per the postmortem report of the deceased he was found intoxicated at the time of accident, therefore, in view of the provisions of Section 185 of MV Act, the below tribunal has rightly held that deceased is liable for negligence in the aforesaid accident.
Hence, the finding given by the below tribunal appears to be correct.
13. In view of the aforesaid, this court is of the considered opinion that the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just and proper.
There is no illegality or perversity found in the impugned award, therefore, no need for any interference.
14. Hence, this miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
C.C. as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Trilok/-
